newsitem.title: USA: US senator says administration to brief on Mexico.
newsitem.headline: US senator says administration to brief on Mexico.

text.p: Clinton administration officials are expected to brief senators on Mexico this week regarding the president's certification of that country as a U.S. ally on fighting drugs, a senator said Tuesday.
"We're going to have a briefing by the administration tomorrow, in the next day or two, to kind of give us their side," Assistant Senate Majority Leader Don Nickles, a Republican from Oklahoma, said.
Clinton certified Mexico as a drug-fighting ally of the United States. A resolution has been introduced in the Senate to decertify Mexico.
Nickles said decertification may not be the best path to take either.

"I'm not positive that is the best way to go," he told reporters, referring to decertification. "There may be a different approach ... some of us are very concerned about Mexico's lack of a real concerted effort on drugs but we're not sure that decertification is absolutely the right way to go," Nickles said.
"So we might try and figure out a way to signal displeasure or a way to signal we want more cooperation, decertification can sometimes be counterproductive," Nickles said.
